name: Mozu-Furuichi Kofun Group: Mounded Tombs of Ancient Japan
description: Rising from the suburbs of Sakai and Habikino near Osaka, this cluster of 49 ancient burial mounds was built between the 3rd and 6th centuries for Japan's elite. Many take the shape of a giant keyhole, surrounded by moats and once decorated with stones and clay figures. The largest, Daisenryo, is thought to have taken about 20 years to build and is traditionally linked to Emperor Nintoku.
